title: Reduced-Round Friet-PC Degree and Cube Attacks
summary: The degree bound was verified through four rounds, with selected degree-32 monomials at five, but attack-relevant degree growth and cube-attack feasibility remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the algebraic degree of Friet-PC and its inverse after 22 or 23 rounds is well below 130, and whether this enables cube attacks against Friet.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of Friet-PC and its inverse for cube attacks against the Friet authenticated-encryption construction.
parameters: 22 or 23 rounds: reduced-round depths under study
130: reference degree threshold for assessing low-degree attack feasibility
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the algebraic degree after 22 or 23 rounds is well below 130, and whether this enables cube attacks against Friet.

citations.label: Friet: an Authenticated Encryption Scheme with Built-in Fault Detection

progress.summary: The paper presents low algebraic degree as a possible route to cube or higher-order differential attacks. It verifies the theoretical upper bound through four rounds and gives selected degree-32 monomials for five rounds, leaving the 22- or 23-round degree behavior unresolved.
citation_labels: Thierry Simon et al., Friet: an Authenticated Encryption Scheme with Built-in Fault Detection
